title: NSIC Rc 732 (Sahod Ulan 37) Rice Variety: Characteristics and Grain Quality
metaTitle: NSIC Rc 732 Rice Variety: Characteristics and Grain Quality
metaDescription: NSIC Rc 732 is an inbred rice for rainfed lowland, approved in 2023. See its pest and disease ratings, grain quality and where it grows best.
excerpt: NSIC Rc 732 is an inbred rice variety for rainfed lowland, known locally as Sahod Ulan 37. The NSIC approved it in 2023. PhilRice bred it. PhilRice has not listed its days to harvest and trial yield yet, but its pest ratings and grain quality are below.

heroImage.alt: Rainfed rice fields from the air, the kind of farm NSIC Rc 732 is meant for

blocks.text: If you came here looking for rice variety 732, or Rc 732, this is the one. The facts below come from PhilRice's catalogue of released varieties, its Binhing Palay app, and its public seed database. So you can compare it with the other varieties in our [rice variety finder](/rice-varieties) before you buy seed. Also read our guide to [rice varieties in the Philippines](/crops/rice-varieties-philippines) for how inbreds, hybrids and special rice differ.

blocks.text: How many days does it take, and how much does it yield?

PhilRice has not published this variety's days to harvest and trial yields in its catalogue yet. So ask the seed seller or your municipal agriculturist for the figures from the trials in your region before you plan the season. Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with the [growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it. Meanwhile, our guide to [raising rice yield per hectare](/blog/increase-rice-yield-per-hectare) covers the habits that matter with any variety.

blocks.text: So scout early for [tungro](/diseases/rice-tungro). When you see the first signs, check the guide before you spray, because the right timing saves more than an extra dose. If you are not sure what you see, our [pest and disease finders](/features/pest-and-disease-finders) help you name it from the damage.

blocks.caption: Grain quality in PhilRice's seed database

blocks.text: Amylose decides how rice cooks. With high amylose, expect rice that is firm and dry, and it hardens as it cools. In fact, PhilRice notes that Filipino taste moved from high to intermediate and low amylose rice, because people want it softer. Head rice is the share of whole grains after milling. So a higher number means fewer broken grains and a better price at the mill.

It suits rainfed lowland that depends on the rains. So wait until the rains settle before you sow the seedbed, then transplant into the puddled field. Our guide to [rice land preparation](/land-preparation/rice-land-preparation) shows each step. For the right month in your province, see [the best time to plant rice](/blog/best-time-to-plant-rice-philippines).

items.q: What is the local name of NSIC Rc 732?
items.a: It is known as Sahod Ulan 37. Seed sellers and agriculturists use both names, so ask for either one.
The NSIC approved it in 2023. PhilRice bred it. PhilRice has not listed its days to harvest and trial yield yet, so ask for the regional trial figures before you plant.
No, it is an inbred. So the seed you buy grows true, but certified seed still gives the best start, as PalayCheck advises.

items.q: What should I watch for when I plant it?
items.a: In PhilRice's tests it was weak against tungro. So scout from the early weeks and act at the first signs.
It has high amylose, 23.2 percent. So it cooks firm and fluffy, and hardens as it cools.

items.q: Where can I buy certified seed of this variety?
items.a: Ask accredited seed growers in your province, your municipal agriculturist or the nearest PhilRice station. Look for the certified seed tag on the sack before you pay.
